analysis:
All three changed files are CI test code for the advisory threat-review scanner. None touches provider, coordinator, cache, attestation or fan-helper code, so no provider threat IDs (T-041, TB-011 and similar) are affected.

Changed behavior covered by tests:
- test-threat-diagnostics.py (head 21-55): canonical_at must resolve the threat model from the exact immutable base SHA (40-hex only), with regular-file and size bounds. Mutable or PR-controlled refs are rejected. Head lines 119-143 add tests for the diagnostics privacy checks.
- test-threat-integration-scope.py (head 97-154): integration receives a bounded exact-source replay. The replay is limited to units the model itself reviewed, so summary text cannot widen the citation scope. Cached source reconstructs the same replay.
- test-threat-model-review.py (head 732-756): the secret-bearing pull_request_target workflow now checks out the scanner from the repository default branch, not the PR base SHA. The base SHA is passed separately as THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA for the canonical model. The tests assert there is no head.sha or head.ref, persist-credentials is false, and the hashed pip install precedes credential acquisition.

Coverage limit: the workflow YAML and the Python modules (context.py, integration_context.py, change_context.py) were not supplied. The tests assert intent only, so I cannot confirm the security properties in the real code. The next pass should check three things in the workflow. First, that the env.THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA fallback for manual runs is validated and not attacker-controlled. Second, that the default-branch scanner checkout never executes PR-head code. Third, that the replayed PR source in the integration prompt (the replay_source output) is treated as untrusted data. No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence.
